observation.visible_scene: A shallow, clear pond viewed from above, filled with emergent aquatic plants (thin green stems topped by yellow and green leaves) and scattered floating leaves. The water surface at the top of the frame carries reflections of pale tree trunks and a standing figure. Several fish are visible beneath the surface: two purplish elongated fish near the center, a pale/white fish and a dark fish near the upper right, and an orange-and-white fish near the upper center. The bottom shows a light sandy substrate with plant shadows.
visible_changes: The camera drifts/pans slowly across the pond (handheld), so the tree-trunk reflections and plant clusters shift toward the right of the frame over the clip, progressively revealing more yellow floating leaves along the left edge.
The two purple fish move gradually to the right relative to the stationary plants, indicating slow swimming rather than only camera motion.
The other fish (pale, dark, orange-and-white) remain roughly in place with only small positional changes tied to the camera drift.
Surface ripples and dappled light patterns change subtly frame to frame; several frames show brief motion blur from the camera movement.
No new objects enter or leave; the plant arrangement itself stays fixed while the viewpoint moves past it.
outside_clip_unknowns: Where the fish are heading and what they are doing beyond this window.
The source of the surface ripples and the full extent of the pond and surrounding bank.
Whether the pale shapes at the top are fish or purely reflections of the sky/trees.
uncertain_details: Separating the fish's own swimming from the camera pan is approximate; the purple fish's rightward drift relative to the plants is the clearest object motion.
The exact identity of the upper pale forms (fish vs. reflection) cannot be confirmed.
Camera motion is a slow lateral drift with minor shake, not a smooth controlled move.
